failure_modes.name: Solver_Passage_Content_Misreading
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 1, the solver states 'From passage [7]: Rousillon Rupes is a scarp on Titania (Uranian moon) named after a character from "All's Well That Ends Well". The scarp was first imaged by Voyager 2 in January 1986.' However, the claim asks whether 'the play...happened before the scarp' - the solver interprets 'happened' to mean when the play was written/created, but 'happened' could refer to the events depicted in the play itself. The solver misreads the claim's temporal reference point.

failure_modes.name: Logical_Reasoning_Error
failure_modes.evidence: The solver concludes the claim is verifiable as true by comparing when the play was written (late 1590s/early 1600s) to when the scarp was imaged (1986). However, the claim states 'the play...happened before the scarp which was first imaged' - this creates a logical confusion. The scarp itself is a geological feature that formed millions of years ago; what 'happened' in 1986 was its imaging by Voyager 2, not the scarp's formation. The solver fails to recognize this ambiguity and treats 'the play happened' as equivalent to 'the play was written,' making an invalid inference about what temporal comparison the claim is actually requesting.
